title: Digital modes: RTTY, FT8 and Winlink
blurb: Choose the right sideband and frequency for digital modes, run FT8 properly, and connect through Winlink gateways.

G2E01.why: RTTY by **AFSK** on an SSB transmitter is normally sent on **LSB**.
G2E01.trap: USB is the sideband for FT8-family modes.

G2E02.why: **VARA** is a digital protocol used with **Winlink**.
G2E02.trap: It isn't EME, direction finding or DX spotting.

G2E03.why: Interference causes **retries and timeouts**, long pauses and failed connections. All of these are symptoms.

G2E04.why: FT8 stations take turns, so pick a **clear frequency** during the **alternate time slot**.
G2E04.trap: Calling in the caller's own slot means you talk over them.

G2E05.why: JT65, JT9, FT4 and FT8 using AFSK use **USB**.

G2E06.why: The most common HF RTTY shift is **170 Hz** between mark and space.

G2E07.why: FT8 slots are strictly timed, so your **computer clock must be within about 1 second**.
G2E07.trap: No special modem is needed. A sound card interface works.

G2E08.why: Most digital activity on 20 m sits **between 14.070 and 14.100 MHz**.
G2E08.trap: SSTV and the top of the phone band are elsewhere.

G2E09.why: A PACTOR connection is between **two stations only**, so you can't join one.

G2E10.why: Send a **connect message** on the gateway's **published frequency**.

G2E11.why: An AREDN mesh provides **high-speed data** during an **emergency or community event**.

G2E12.why: Winlink is a wireless email network, a form of packet radio, and works on VHF and HF. **All** are true.

G2E13.why: A Winlink Remote Message Server is a **gateway** between radio and the internet.
G2E13.trap: A TNC is a radio modem, not a server.

G2E14.why: **Reversed mark/space**, **wrong baud rate** and **wrong sideband** each stop decoding. All can be the cause.

G2E15.why: FT8 on 20 m sits at about **14.074 to 14.077 MHz**, inside the digital segment.
G2E15.trap: 14.110 to 14.113 is above the digital segment.
